meta.notice: Every person, run, value and finding here is invented for mockups. Genes and drug rules are real so the copy reads plausibly; positions, read counts, scores and dates are made up. Do not look any of it up as if it described someone.

levels.act: Take to a doctor. A health finding with a clinical action (dominant P/LP in an ACMG SF or cancer gene, two hits in a recessive gene, a full repeat expansion, a positive MUC1 call).
levels.medicine: Tell whoever prescribes. A gene result that changes a drug or dose under CPIC guidance, or an HLA drug allele.
levels.review: Worth a look. A result that deserves a conversation or a measurement but is not a diagnosis (intermediate repeat, genetically high Lp(a), CHIP clone, mosaic alteration, risk-associated HLA allele).
levels.carrier: For family planning. One copy of a change in a recessive or X-linked gene; the person is not affected.
levels.info: For information. Ancestry, haplogroups, traits, blood groups, scores, telomeres. Never phrased as fine or normal.
levels.trust: About the data, not the person: QC, identity, contamination, callability, relationships.

meta.never: No result is ever shown as 'all clear', 'normal' or 'fine'. An empty section reads 'No finding in what this step assessed' plus its caveat and what it does not see.

found_so_far.text: Sex from the reads XY, declared male. Contamination 0.2% (below 3%).
Mean depth 34.1x; 97.8% of the genome at 10x or more.
2 pathogenic or likely pathogenic ClinVar hits, both heterozygous in recessive genes.
HLA typed: no drug-reaction allele of the list present.

rows.explanation: Both carry a change in CFTR. A child who inherits both changes can have cystic fibrosis: 1 in 4 per pregnancy, 1 in 2 a carrier, 1 in 4 neither.
Only Marc carries a change in PAH. A child can be a carrier like Marc, not affected, unless Elena carries a change this screen does not see.
Only Elena carries a change in HFE. A child can be a carrier like Elena.
Elena's longer allele is in the intermediate range: below the 55 repeats the screen counts. It does not cause disease but may grow by a few repeats when passed on. Shown for context.

smn1.note: Two copies do not rule out a silent carrier (2+0).

couple_screen.caveat: A screen, not a diagnosis. It sees ClinVar pathogenic changes, Delly deletions, SMN1 copies and FMR1/FXN repeats in 3,292 recessive and X-linked genes. A screen with no shared gene lowers the chance of a child with one of these conditions; it does not remove it.
does_not_see: changes ClinVar does not list as pathogenic (new loss-of-function changes, VUS)
SMN1 silent carriers (2 copies on one chromosome, 0 on the other)
genes with a near-identical copy: HBA1/HBA2, CYP21A2, GBA1
repeat expansions other than FMR1 and FXN
low-level mosaicism, and whether two changes of one person sit on the same copy

inheritance_of_findings.sensitive: adult-onset finding about a minor: keep behind an explicit reveal

inheritance_of_findings.how: repeat length (48 in Elena, 49 in Lía)

de_novo.note: Most de novo candidates of a whole genome are genotype errors; this one has good depth in all three. No gene nearby.

compound_het.note: Both came from Marc on one copy; the other copy is intact.
Both rare missense, both called benign or VUS. TTN is huge and carries many rare missense in everyone; no action.

findings.title: A change in BRCA2 linked to hereditary breast and ovarian cancer
findings.acmg_sf_rule: dominant gene: one P/LP variant is reported
findings.what_it_means: One copy of BRCA2 carries a change that stops the protein early. People with such a change have a higher lifetime risk of breast and ovarian cancer, and to a smaller degree prostate and pancreatic cancer in male relatives. It is not a diagnosis of cancer.
findings.what_to_do: Bring this to a doctor or genetic counsellor. Confirm it with a clinical test. Screening and prevention options exist and start earlier than the general programme. Close relatives (parents, siblings, children) each have a 1 in 2 chance of carrying it.
findings.relatives: Lía did not inherit this change (family analysis). Elena's mother Carmen is not sequenced.
findings.caveat: A research pipeline, not a clinical test. Confirm every pathogenic finding in a certified laboratory before acting.

findings.title: Carrier of cystic fibrosis
findings.what_it_means: One copy of CFTR carries the most common cystic fibrosis change. Carriers are not affected.
findings.what_to_do: Matters for children: Marc also carries a CFTR change (couple screen: shared, 1 in 4).
findings.caveat: Carrier status is not disease.

findings.title: FMR1 repeat in the intermediate range
findings.what_it_means: One copy of FMR1 has 48 CGG repeats: more than usual, below a premutation. It does not cause disease but can grow by a few repeats when passed to a child.
findings.what_to_do: Worth a word with a genetic counsellor before a future pregnancy. Lía inherited this allele (49 repeats).
findings.caveat: Repeat sizing from short reads is approximate; a long expansion cannot be sized.

findings.title: CYP2D6: intermediate metaboliser
findings.consensus: pypgx and Cyrius agree, depth check ok

drugs.cpic: Consider an aromatase inhibitor for postmenopausal women, or a higher tamoxifen dose (40 mg/day); avoid strong CYP2D6 inhibitors.
Use label-recommended dosing; if no response, consider a non-tramadol opioid.
No action needed for intermediate metabolisers.

findings.what_to_do: Show the medicines list to whoever prescribes. Tamoxifen is relevant to the BRCA2 finding.
findings.caveat: CYP2D6 is hard for short reads; the pipeline passes it to PharmCAT only when two callers agree. Confirm with a certified PGx test before a prescription changes.

findings.title: Carrier of hereditary haemochromatosis (HFE C282Y, one copy)
findings.acmg_sf_rule: HFE is reported only when homozygous C282Y: this is not a secondary finding.
findings.what_it_means: One copy. Iron overload is rare with one copy.
findings.caveat: Carrier status is not disease.

findings.title: Breast cancer polygenic score: 71st percentile
findings.what_it_means: Higher than 71 of 100 reference people of similar ancestry. A percentile is not a probability.
findings.caveat: Scores of different conditions are not comparable. With a BRCA2 change, the BRCA2 result guides care, not this score.

findings.title: APOE genotype (hidden until you choose to see it)
findings.gate_text: APOE relates to the risk of late-onset Alzheimer's disease. Many people choose not to know. Show it?
findings.what_it_means: One ε4 allele raises the risk of late-onset Alzheimer's disease; it does not say who will get it.
findings.caveat: No prevention changes on APOE alone.

findings.title: Maternal line: haplogroup H1c3
findings.what_it_means: The branch of the maternal line's tree; H is the most common in Western Europe. Lía carries the same haplogroup, as expected.
findings.caveat: Haplogroup associations with disease are population statistics, not individual predictions.

findings.title: Genetic ancestry most similar to Southern European reference groups
findings.caveat: Similarity to reference groups, not a population label or a nationality.

findings.title: Data quality: good enough to read
findings.what_it_means: Depth and quality are in the usual range; no sign of another person's DNA; the sex from the reads matches. A 'no finding' in the genes listed as hard to read says nothing.

findings.title: CYP2C19: poor metaboliser

drugs.cpic: Avoid. Use prasugrel or ticagrelor if there is no contraindication.
Consider a 50% lower starting dose and slower titration, or another antidepressant.
Start at the standard dose; for long-term use consider a 50% lower daily dose.
Choose an alternative antifungal not dependent on CYP2C19.

findings.what_to_do: Tell any prescriber and pharmacist. Clopidogrel is the important one: it would not work well.
findings.caveat: PharmCAT is a research tool; confirm before a prescription changes.

findings.title: SLCO1B1: decreased function (statin muscle side effects)

drugs.cpic: Prescribe 20 mg/day or less, or choose another statin (rosuvastatin, pravastatin).
Prescribe 40 mg/day or less; consider a higher dose only with monitoring.

findings.what_to_do: Relevant together with the Lp(a) and heart-score results: if a statin is started, the choice and dose matter.
findings.caveat: Confirm before a prescription changes.

findings.title: Genetically high Lp(a) likely
findings.population_range_note: most people carry 30 to 45 KIV-2 copies in total; fewer copies go with higher Lp(a)
findings.what_it_means: Few KIV-2 repeats and one risk variant both point to a high Lp(a), a lipoprotein that raises the risk of heart attack and aortic stenosis.
findings.what_to_do: Ask for one blood Lp(a) measurement. European guidance recommends measuring it once in every adult anyway.
findings.caveat: A research estimate from read depth; the blood test is what counts.

findings.title: Coronary artery disease score: 88th percentile
findings.what_it_means: Higher than 88 of 100 reference people of similar ancestry. Most people in the top fifth never have a heart attack; measured LDL, blood pressure and Lp(a) say far more.
findings.caveat: A percentile is not a probability; percentiles of different conditions are not comparable.

findings.title: Carrier of cystic fibrosis
findings.what_to_do: Shared with Elena: 1 in 4 per pregnancy for cystic fibrosis. Lía did not inherit this one.

findings.title: Carrier of phenylketonuria
HLA-B*27 present
findings.what_it_means: About 8% of Europeans carry HLA-B*27; most never develop spondylitis. Coeliac DQ2.5 is common too (about 1 in 4) and alone means little.
findings.caveat: Typing from short reads is approximate; ask for a clinical HLA test before a drug that depends on it. Not for transplant matching.

findings.title: One uncertain deletion; no class 4-5 structural variant
findings.what_it_means: A 38 kb deletion inside an intron, found by three callers. Uncertain significance: no action.
findings.caveat: Short reads find large deletions and duplications better than insertions and inversions.

findings.title: No CHIP call above what this depth can see
findings.what_it_means: No clone was found in the 13 CHIP genes, but at 29x only clones with about 14% of reads or more can be seen. Most CHIP is smaller.
findings.caveat: A clean result does not rule CHIP out.

findings.title: Paternal line: R-DF27
findings.what_it_means: DF27 is the commonest Y branch in Iberia.
findings.caveat: One line out of thousands of ancestors.

findings.title: Data quality: good, one step not assessed
findings.failed: Step 52 MUC1 VNTR: depth over the repeat 41x, below the 100x it needs: not assessed.

findings.title: Carrier of cystic fibrosis (from Elena)
findings.what_it_means: Lía carries one copy, from her mother, and is not affected. She did not inherit Marc's CFTR change, so the 1 in 4 did not happen for her.
findings.what_to_do: Matters for her own children one day.

findings.title: FMR1 repeat in the intermediate range (from Elena)
findings.what_it_means: Lía's maternal allele grew from 48 to 49 repeats. Still intermediate; it does not cause disease.
findings.caveat: Short-read sizing is approximate: a one-repeat change is within the error.

findings.title: CYP2C19: intermediate metaboliser

drugs.cpic: Avoid standard dose; use an alternative antiplatelet if possible.
Start at the standard dose; consider a lower dose for long-term use.

findings.caveat: Genes PharmCAT could not call are listed apart; absence from the drug list does not mean normal function.

findings.title: Predicted blood group O, RhD negative

systems.genotype: RHD deleted / RHD deleted (copies by depth 0.04)

findings.what_it_means: Both parents are RhD positive with one RHD-deleted copy each; Lía inherited both deleted copies.
findings.caveat: A prediction from DNA, not a serological typing. For a transfusion the lab types the blood.

findings.title: 1 de novo candidate that passes filters, outside any gene
findings.what_it_means: Every child carries a few dozen new changes; most candidates here are genotype errors. This one sits outside genes.
findings.caveat: Confirm a de novo change that matters by another method.

findings.title: Elena and Marc both carry a cystic fibrosis change
findings.what_it_means: Each pregnancy: 1 in 4 affected, 1 in 2 carrier, 1 in 4 neither. Lía is a carrier, not affected.
findings.what_to_do: Before another pregnancy, a genetic counsellor can explain options (clinical carrier confirmation, prenatal or preimplantation testing).

findings.title: Family relationships match the pedigree
findings.what_it_means: Each declared parent-child pair measures about 0.5; the partners measure unrelated. No sample swap.

not_assessed_everyone: Changes ClinVar does not list, unless another step ranks them
Genes short reads cannot place (see the callability list of each person)
Long repeat expansions beyond read length (only a lower bound)
Somatic changes below about 10% of reads
